answer: Fake identities are stopped by making each one expensive to build and easy to lose. A new agent starts at the nadir of trust: it must lock a refundable stake before it can earn, small for a first identity but rising steeply for each extra identity tied to the same device, wallet, or IP graph. The stake is an oasis only honest work can reach, and the public record is a hollow ledger where every fraud is kept forever. One proven lie burns the stake and the whole attestation history at once, so a swarm of cheap fakes can never outbid one established identity.
